Definition: irregular feminine of G1520; one or first:--a (certain), + agree, first, one, X other.
BiblicalUsage: Not one jot or one tittle shall pass from the law till all is fulfilled, Jesus says, and the women came to the tomb very early on the first day of the week. The word is the feminine of one, a single one or the first one, and it carries the smallest mark of the law and the first morning of the week.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that one jot is the measure of God's faithfulness: if not even the smallest stroke of the law falls, then not one of His promises will fail either.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
